operation_tail.detail: The ONSPD also contains Channel Islands and Isle of Man postcodes; this England shard filters territory explicitly rather than assuming every directory row is English.
England candidates require the documented country code E92000001; postcode text or coordinate position alone is not used to infer country.
The record specification allows blank national-grid fields for Channel Islands and Isle of Man postcodes, preventing null coordinates from being misclassified as malformed England rows.
Northern Ireland postcode grid references use the Irish National Grid; they are excluded from the England British National Grid transformation path.
Administrative, electoral and health geography joins require the documented nine-character GSS codes.
Geography names are resolved from the accompanying ONS lookup files; code-to-name values are not guessed from prefixes.
Stable geography codes are retained as join keys while names remain descriptive attributes that may change.
USERTYPE is validated as 0 for small user or 1 for large user; other values fail closed.
Small-user and large-user classifications are not interpreted as an address count or a one-postcode-to-one-premise relationship.
OSEAST1M is checked against the documented numeric-or-null schema and retained at its stated one-metre grid-reference resolution.
OSNRTH1M is checked against the documented numeric-or-null schema and is not populated by inference when absent.
OSGRDIND accepts only documented values 1 through 6, 8 or 9; value 7 and other unexpected codes are rejected.
Postcodes terminated since November 2000 retain the positional-quality indicator held before termination; termination alone does not reset the code.
For PQI 8 records terminated before Gridlink, England and Wales grid references are mainly 100-metre resolution and are not presented as one-metre parcel evidence.
Where no grid reference exists, dependent administrative and statistical geography fields may be blank and are not backfilled from nearby postcodes.
England OA21 values must use the documented E00 code family and nine-character form.
England LSOA21 values must use the documented E01 code family and nine-character form.
England MSOA21 values must use the documented E02 code family and nine-character form.
OA21 is allowed to be blank when the postcode has no grid reference; null is not converted into a fabricated output area.
LSOA21 is allowed to be blank when the postcode has no grid reference; no neighbouring-area imputation is performed.
MSOA21 is allowed to be blank when the postcode has no grid reference and remains unavailable rather than inferred.
Pseudo codes reserved for other UK nations and Crown Dependencies are not accepted as valid England geography assignments.
ONSPD release news can add or remove geography fields, so the parser records the release version and validates headers instead of assuming a permanent schema.
The documented ONSPD_MMM_YYYY_UK naming pattern is used to bind parsed rows to an explicit month and year.
CSV and fixed-format ASCII distributions are distinct representations; one is not parsed using the other's delimiter or record rules.
Canonical postcode files are sourced from the documented Open Geography distribution route and retain release provenance.
The February 2025 FOI attachment is used for field methodology only and does not replace a current ONSPD release for lifecycle status.
The Gridlink core lineage is recorded across Royal Mail, Ordnance Survey, National Records of Scotland, Land and Property Services and ONS.
Most GB postcode grid references derive from OS AddressBase address coordinates; this source lineage is retained without claiming a parcel survey.
New postcode coordinates may begin as ONS-imputed values and later be replaced by improved AddressBase-derived references.
Latitude and longitude are derived by transforming easting and northing and therefore do not count as an independent coordinate confirmation.
GB administrative and electoral assignments use postcode grid references against Boundary-Line through point-in-polygon processing.
The May ONSPD can use a draft Boundary-Line release while corrections from the final release feed the November ONSPD; vintage-specific assignments are preserved.
ONS warns that individual-address allocation can be imprecise because of straddling and imputation; postcode geography is not promoted to exact parcel proof.
Visual inspection confirmed USERTYPE, easting, northing, positional-quality, OA21/LSOA21/MSOA21 and distribution-format specifications.
The official Spring page reports a 32.2 MB ZIP; this compressed transfer size is kept separate from documented uncompressed member totals.
The archive must preserve separate postcode_files and postcode_res_files member groups rather than flattening or mixing their revisions.
Every all-premises postcode member must follow the documented 202601_fixed_postcode_coverage_r2_XX.csv pattern.
Strict validation requires 121 all-premises r2 members representing 121 unique postcode areas.
The combined all-premises postcode member row count must equal the official total of 1,741,096.
The residential r1 postcode members have a separate official total of 1,606,191 and are not added to the all-premises join.
postcode and postcode_space are normalized to the same identity while preserving the original fields for audit.
Because Ofcom states that fields may appear in a different order, required columns are resolved by exact header name rather than position.
Postcode-level premise-count fields absent from the official schema are not synthesized from percentages or external address estimates.

Forty-five official record-schema, geography-code, coordinate, release-format and archive-topology controls were published line by line; exact coverage candidates remain blocked until strict r2 byte validation.
